In order for a lightning protection system (LPS) to maintain its conformity to BS EN 62305 or BS 6651 it should be tested regularly and inspected to ensure that no defect develops which may affect the operational capacity of the system.
The objective of the inspection is to ascertain that:
• The LPS conforms to the design based on the standard,
• All components of the LPS are in good condition and capable of performing their designed functions and that there is
no corrosion,
• Any recently added services or constructions are incorporated into the LPS.
These tests should be carried out in accordance with Section 7 of BS EN62305/3 2006, older systems should be tested under section 32 of BS6651 1999.
As the resistance of the earth electrodes can be affected by changing climactic conditions such as ground frosts, drought or heavy rainfall it is beneficial to test the system at various times of the year, by testing at intervals of 11 months over a 10 year period the earthing results can be monitored in all seasons and ground conditions.
We would therefore recommend that this system be tested annually at 11 month intervals. Intervals should not exceed 12 months. Testing should also be carried out if the system is struck by lightning irrespective of the scheduled test date.
